title: Compatible comparison after completing original levels in the second ideal
statement: Let X be Noetherian, I,K quasi-coherent ideals and M in Coh(X,I), N in Coh(X,K), F,H coherent [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Let alpha:M -> completion_I H and delta:N -> completion_K H. Suppose sigma is an isomorphism of double diagrams N_e/I^(n+1)N_e -> M_n/K^(e+1)M_n, natural in e,n. Suppose theta:(H/K^(e+1)H)/I^(n+1) -> (H/I^(n+1)H)/K^(e+1) is natural and carries the composite projection from H to the composite projection in the other order. Assume sigma followed by reduction of alpha_n equals reduction of delta_e followed by theta. Let a:F -> H, beta:N isomorphic to completion_K F with delta=beta.hom followed by completion_K(a). Then there is an isomorphism Xi, natural in n, between the K-completion of the I-reductions of F and the K-completion of the levels M_n. For every n its forward map followed by completion_K(alpha_n) equals completion_K(a modulo I^(n+1)). No torsion or algebraization hypothesis is used.

proof.text: Apply grothendieckDevissage_secondAdicSystem_comparison to F.obj to obtain the natural interchange tau and its composite-projection equation. This reuses the existing cokernel construction rather than constructing a second interchange.

source.place: Tag 088A (lemma-existence-tricky), final paragraph, reduction of beta modulo I^n

proof.text: Forget beta to an isomorphism b of K-completion diagrams. Whisker b.inverse by the I-completion functor and compose with sigma. Precompose with tau.inverse, then apply the flip functor to this composite isomorphism. Since flipping twice is definitionally the identity, this gives Xi with exactly the required source and target, natural in both indices.

source.place: Tag 088A (lemma-existence-tricky), final paragraph, reduction of beta modulo I^n

proof.text: At every pair of indices prove tau.forward followed by K-reduction of I-reduction of a equals I-reduction of K-reduction of a followed by the supplied theta. Cancel the two epimorphic quotient projections from F. Use the projection equation for tau, the cokernel equations for the reduced maps, and the supplied projection equation htheta precomposed by a. This proves the needed module-map naturality without choosing an interchange for H or a witness for any coherent module.

source.place: Tag 088A (lemma-existence-tricky), final paragraph, reduction of beta modulo I^n

proof.text: The equation hbeta and the inverse law for b give b.inverse at e followed by delta at e equal to K-reduction of a. Expand Xi componentwise. Substitute the supplied comparison square hsquare, combine the two I-reduction maps using formalModuleQuotientMap_comp, and substitute this equality. Use the naturality equation from the preceding step and cancel tau.inverse followed by tau.forward. Two applications of NatTrans.ext identify the full diagram maps.

lean.statement:
theorem grothendieckDevissage_completedComparison
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I K : X.IdealSheafData)
    (M : CoherentFormalModule X I) (H : CoherentModules X)
    (α : M ⟶ (completion X I).obj H)
    (N : CoherentFormalModule X K) (δ : N ⟶ (completion X K).obj H)
    (σ : N.obj ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor I ≅ (M.obj ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor K).flip)
    (θ : formalCompletionSystem K H.obj ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor I ≅
      (formalCompletionSystem I H.obj ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor K).flip)
    (hθ : ∀ e n : ℕ,
      formalModuleQuotientπ K (e + 1) H.obj ≫
        formalModuleQuotientπ I (n + 1) (formalModuleQuotient K (e + 1) H.obj) ≫
        (θ.hom.app (op e)).app (op n) =
      formalModuleQuotientπ I (n + 1) H.obj ≫
        formalModuleQuotientπ K (e + 1) (formalModuleQuotient I (n + 1) H.obj))
    (hsquare : ∀ e n : ℕ,
      (σ.hom.app (op e)).app (op n) ≫
        formalModuleQuotientMap K (α.hom.app (op n)) (Nat.le_refl (e + 1)) =
      formalModuleQuotientMap I (δ.hom.app (op e)) (Nat.le_refl (n + 1)) ≫
        (θ.hom.app (op e)).app (op n))
    (F : CoherentModules X) (a : F ⟶ H) (β : N ≅ (completion X K).obj F)
    (hβ : δ = β.hom ≫ (completion X K).map a) :
    ∃ Ξ : ((completion X I).obj F).obj ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor K ≅
        M.obj ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor K,
      ∀ n : ℕᵒᵖ,
        Ξ.hom.app n ≫ formalCompletionMap K (α.hom.app n) =
          formalCompletionMap K (((completion X I).map a).hom.app n)
